note: The exact route-table change PTF-FIRECRAWL-HARD-LANES-003 would justify, written out so it can be reviewed before anything is edited. routes.json is untouched and Firecrawl remains unregistered. Applying this is a separate work order.

what_the_measurement_supports.CHOICE: 3/3 acquired, 3/3 publication-grade, 3/3 complete, 0 structured mismatches, 0 false facts, 20.8s against the Bright Data Choice lane's measured 130.0s. The richest structured case matched on all 9 fields including fee amount, basis, scope, weight, count and count scope; both captured no-pets refusals were preserved exactly.
what_the_measurement_supports.MARRIOTT: 1/4 acquired and that one was incomplete (4 fields down to 3). The other three returned SCRAPE_ALL_ENGINES_FAILED. Aloft also FAILED on an earlier identical run, so even the single success is not reliable.

what_the_measurement_does_NOT_support: Firecrawl as a default provider. It cannot reach Marriott or Hilton at all, and those two carry 54 of Milwaukee's 127 routable rows.

Firecrawl as a first lane with Bright Data fallback on Marriott or Hilton. A first lane that fails ~90% of the time on those brands spends a credit and 30-50 seconds to learn nothing, and delays every property behind it.

A claim that Firecrawl extends Choice coverage. It does not. The three Country Inn & Suites by Radisson properties the Web Unlocker cannot reach were tested separately and Firecrawl failed all three with the same SCRAPE_ALL_ENGINES_FAILED. Same coverage, not better coverage.

step_1_register_the_provider.change: register a `firecrawl` provider backed by scripts/pettripfinder/acquisition/firecrawl_capture.py, with capabilities {runs_javascript, geo_pinnable} and cost metadata measured in plan credits rather than usd_minor.
step_1_register_the_provider.also_required: move `firecrawl` out of KNOWN_FUTURE_PROVIDERS, and update tests/pettripfinder/acquisition/test_acquisition_router.py::test_two_providers_are_implemented_and_one_slot_is_reserved and ::test_future_providers_are_documented_and_not_implemented, which currently assert it is NOT implemented. Those assertions are correct today and must be changed deliberately, not deleted.

after.why: 3/3 acquired at 20.8s against the Web Unlocker's measured 130.0s on the same lane, with zero structured mismatches and both no-pets refusals preserved. The Web Unlocker stays as fallback because it is proven at 11/15 on this lane and nothing here retires it.

step_2_route_choice.unchanged_and_deliberate: forbidden_providers keeps brightdata_browser. That rule was bought with fourteen refusals in fifteen attempts and no result here touches it.

step_3_domain_row.change: mirror the CHOICE brand row, so a Choice property whose brand is unknown takes the same lane.

step_4_leave_alone.WYNDHAM: unchanged in this proposal. Benchmark-002 measured Firecrawl favourably on Wyndham (it recovered a full policy where the incumbent returned a heading), but that was a different work order's sample and Wyndham is not in this decision test. It deserves its own before being moved.

validation_required_before_applying: The Choice sample here is n=3. Run the remaining Choice properties in the Milwaukee queue (15 in total) through Firecrawl and require the same result: zero structured mismatches and no false pets_allowed or no_pets.
Confirm the fallback actually fires: force a Firecrawl failure on a Choice property and verify the router falls through to brightdata_web_unlocker rather than reporting the property unreachable.

Confirm credit accounting under load. This run consumed 4 credits for 4 successful acquisitions and was charged nothing for the 12 failed scrape calls, but that is an observation over one small run, not a billing guarantee.
risk_if_applied_as_written: Low and bounded. Choice keeps its proven provider as a fallback, so the worst case is a wasted Firecrawl call before the current behaviour resumes. The failure mode that would matter -- a wrong policy fact -- did not occur once in this test, and the no-pets cases, where a wrong answer is most damaging, were reproduced exactly.
superseded_note: Decision C here rested on the belief that Firecrawl only matched Choice coverage. Completing the fifteen-property sample disproved that: it reaches seven Choice properties the production run does not hold. The 004 proposal supersedes this one at decision B. Neither has been applied.
